title: Raw and Byte Strings
goal: Write raw string literals and binary byte slices.

sections.text: You use raw string literals in Python or C++ to avoid escaping backslashes. Rust provides raw string literals and byte string literals for the same purpose.

sections.code:
let raw = r"C:\notes\new";
let bytes = b"hello";
sections.caption: Raw strings ignore escapes. Byte strings are byte slices.

sections.text: Raw strings start with `r"` or `r#"` and end with `"` or `"#`. You add matching hashes on both ends when your text contains double quote characters.

sections.code:
let json = r#"{"status": "ok"}"#;
let header: &[u8] = b"HTTP/1.1";
sections.caption: Hashes allow inner quotes. The b prefix makes a byte slice.

sections.text: A byte string literal `b"..."` creates a byte slice `&[u8]`. It contains raw ASCII bytes rather than UTF-8 `&str` text.

explanation: Write raw string literals and binary byte slices.
